terms.definition: The rate at which work is done — energy transferred each second.
terms.function: Speed of energy, from sprint bursts to load gauges.
terms.whereItIs: The watt meter on the lift rig.
terms.whyItMatters: Every engine, bulb, and athlete is rated by share power

terms.definition: The formula that divides total work by the time taken.
terms.whyItMatters: One formula lets you compare a sprinter and a plodder doing identical jobs.
terms.whereItIs: The dial readout while the belt moves.

terms.definition: The SI unit of power: one joule per second.
terms.whyItMatters: Sticker wattages, battery charging rates, and kilowatt-hours all use it.

terms.definition: The same work finished in less time stands at a higher power
terms.whyItMatters: Explains sprinters out-blasting hikers and turbo kettles over slow-boilers.
terms.whereItIs: The speed knob and its spike in the watt readout.
